Frasers Aims to Increase Hugo Boss Stake Above 50%
Frasers Group said it aims to increase its stake in premium fashion company Hugo Boss to more than 50%, as it weighs its support for the German company's chairman.
Last month, the British retail company--founded by billionaire Mike Ashley--said it now holds 33.05 million shares in Hugo Boss, or 47.89%, after the acceptance period for its offer ended.
In June, Frasers launched an offer to buy the stake in Hugo Boss it didn't already own for 1.93 billion euros ($2.24 billion).
On Tuesday, Frasers said it plans to further increase its interest in the company, including through the purchase of more shares. The company said its intention is to build an interest above 50%.
Frasers said it is also reviewing whether it will continue to support Stephan Sturm as chairman of Hugo Boss's supervisory board.
Hugo Boss didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
